nameStory: The Willow Leaf Beetle earned its name from its favorite dining spots - willow trees! These tiny beetles spend most of their lives munching on willow leaves, making them easy to find wherever willows grow. The scientific name 'versicolora' means 'changing colors,' hinting at this beetle's ability to shift hues as it matures.
description: The Willow Leaf Beetle is a small, oval-shaped beetle that's part of the large leaf beetle family. These compact insects are typically metallic-looking with a shiny, dome-like shell that covers their back. Adults are quite small, usually measuring just a few millimeters long - about the size of a large pinhead. They're often found in groups on willow trees, where both adults and larvae feed on the leaves.

idTips.label: Metallic sheen
idTips.description: The wing covers have a distinctive metallic luster that catches the light, often appearing bronze, copper, or greenish depending on the angle and age of the beetle

idTips.label: Oval body shape
idTips.description: The body is distinctly oval and dome-shaped when viewed from above, like a tiny football cut in half lengthwise

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Very small at just 3-5 millimeters long - about the size of a pencil eraser or small bead

idTips.label: Smooth texture
idTips.description: The wing covers feel smooth and hard to the touch, like polished metal, with no obvious bumps or ridges

idTips.label: Willow association
idTips.description: Almost always found on or near willow trees and shrubs, often in small groups on the undersides of leaves

habitat: Look for Willow Leaf Beetles anywhere willows grow in New England - along streams, pond edges, wetlands, and low-lying areas with moist soil. They're especially common near black willows, weeping willows, and native willow shrubs. You'll also find them in parks, yards, and gardens where ornamental willows are planted.

seasonality.spring: Adults emerge from overwintering sites and begin feeding on newly emerging willow leaves. This is when you're most likely to see them actively moving and mating on willow branches.
seasonality.summer: Peak activity period with both adults and larvae feeding on willow foliage. Look for small holes chewed in willow leaves as evidence of their presence.
seasonality.fall: Adults prepare for winter by seeking shelter under bark, in leaf litter, or other protected spots. Feeding activity slows as temperatures drop.
seasonality.winter: Adults overwinter in protected locations and are rarely seen. Look for them under loose bark or in deep leaf litter during mild winter days.

funFact: Despite their tiny size, Willow Leaf Beetles can completely strip the leaves from small willow branches when they gather in large numbers, yet the trees almost always recover completely and the beetles rarely cause permanent damage!
confusionNotes: These beetles can be confused with other small metallic leaf beetles, but their strong association with willows is the best clue. If you find small, shiny beetles on any tree other than a willow, you're probably looking at a different species. Remember: 'Willows and metallic shine - Willow Leaf Beetles every time!'
compareHints: Since this is the only Plagiodera species in our region, compare it to other small leaf beetles in the Chrysomelidae family. Unlike flea beetles that jump when disturbed, Willow Leaf Beetles tend to drop or crawl away slowly. They're also more consistently metallic than many other leaf beetles, which may be solid colors without the shiny luster.
